propositions.text: The appellant is a citizen of DRC and Rwanda appealing the RPD's rejection of his refugee claim under IRPA section 97.
propositions.quote: The appellant, XXXX XXXX XXXX, is a citizen of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and of Rwanda. He is appealing against the decision of the Refugee Protection Division (RPD) rejecting his claim for refugee protection by determining that he is neither a "Convention refugee" nor a "person in need of protection" under section 97 of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA).

paragraphs.summary: The appellant, a DRC and Rwanda citizen, appeals the RPD's rejection of his refugee claim under IRPA section 97, says the court.

propositions.text: The appellant submitted no new evidence and did not request a hearing before the RAD.
propositions.quote: The appellant did not submit any new evidence in support of his appeal. He did not ask to be heard before the Refugee Appeal Division (RAD).

paragraphs.summary: The appellant submitted no new evidence and did not request a hearing before the RAD, says the court.

propositions.text: The appellant requests the RAD to allow the appeal and grant a favorable decision or refer the matter to the RPD for redetermination by another panel.
propositions.quote: He is requesting that the RAD allow the appeal and render a favourable decision. In the alternative, he is requesting that the RAD to refer the matter to the RPD for redetermination of his refugee protection claim by another panel.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant requests the RAD to allow the appeal or refer the matter to the RPD for redetermination, says the appellant.

propositions.text: The Minister did not intervene in the appeal.
propositions.quote: The Minister did not intervene in the appeal.

paragraphs.summary: The Minister did not intervene in the appeal, says the respondent.

propositions.text: Pursuant to IRPA subsection 111(1), the RAD confirms the RPD's determination that the appellant is neither a Convention refugee nor a person in need of protection.
propositions.quote: Pursuant to subsection 111(1) of the IRPA, the RAD confirms the determination of the RPD, namely, that XXXX XXXX XXXX is neither a "Convention refugee" nor a "person in need of protection" within the meaning of section 97 of the IRPA.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD confirms the RPD's determination that the appellant is neither a Convention refugee nor a person in need of protection, says the court.

propositions.text: The appeal is dismissed.
propositions.quote: The appeal is dismissed.

paragraphs.summary: The appeal is dismissed, says the court.

propositions.text: The claimant alleges facts in his Basis of Claim Form (BOC Form).
propositions.quote: In his Basis of Claim Form (BOC Form), the refugee protection claimant alleges the following.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant alleges facts in his Basis of Claim Form, says the court.

propositions.text: The claimant is a Tutsi born in DRC, lived in Rwanda for education, obtained Rwandan citizenship in 2008, and worked under XXXX XXXX XXXX.
propositions.quote: He is a XXXX Tutsi born in the DRC. He went to live in Rwanda to complete his education. In 2008, he obtained Rwandan citizenship and found a job in the XXXX XXXX XXXX under the XXXX XXXX XXXX.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant is a Tutsi born in DRC, lived in Rwanda, obtained citizenship in 2008, and worked under XXXX XXXX XXXX, says the RPD.

propositions.text: In 2009, RPF officials asked the claimant to become an informant; he pretended to accept but left his job.
propositions.quote: In 2009, the XXXX of the Rwandan Patriotic Front (RPF) and a XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX asked him to become an informant. He allegedly acted as though he accepted, but he left his job.

paragraphs.summary: In 2009, RPF officials asked the claimant to be an informant; he pretended to accept but left his job, says the RPD.

propositions.text: In 2010, he began working for XXXX XXXX XXXX and acted as a XXXX for XXXX XXXX XXXX.
propositions.quote: On XXXX XXXX XXXX 2010, he began working for the XXXX XXXX XXXX and also acted as a XXXX for XXXX XXXX XXXX.

paragraphs.summary: In 2010, he began working for XXXX XXXX XXXX and acted as a XXXX for XXXX XXXX XXXX, says the RPD.

propositions.text: In 2010, members of XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX arrested, detained, and tortured him for three days to get information about a plot.
propositions.quote: The claimant alleged that on XXXX XXXX XXXX 2010, members of the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX arrested, detained and tortured him for three days to obtain information about a plot by XXXX XXXX XXXX and XXXX soldiers from the DRC.

paragraphs.summary: In 2010, members of XXXX XXXX XXXX arrested, detained, and tortured him for three days to get information about a plot, says the RPD.

propositions.text: In 2013, he was held and interrogated at the border by Rwandan authorities and threatened with reprisals several times afterwards.
propositions.quote: On XXXX XXXX, 2013, on his way back from the DRC, he was held and interrogated at the border by Rwandan authorities about his alleged ties to XXXX XXXX. The claimant alleged that, in the months that followed, he was threatened with reprisals on several occasions.

paragraphs.summary: In 2013, he was held and interrogated at the border and threatened with reprisals several times, says the RPD.

propositions.text: In 2014, he changed jobs hoping to avoid problems.
propositions.quote: On XXXX XXXX XXXX 2014, he allegedly changed jobs, hoping to avoid problems.

paragraphs.summary: In 2014, he changed jobs hoping to avoid problems, says the RPD.

propositions.text: In 2015, he was attacked and beaten but saved by passersby; police did not investigate after hospital release.
propositions.quote: He alleged that on XXXX XXXX XXXX 2015, when he was out for a walk, he was attacked and savagely beaten. He was saved by the shouts of passersby. On his release from hospital, he asked the police to investigate the incident, but nothing was done.

paragraphs.summary: In 2015, he was attacked and beaten but saved by passersby; police did not investigate, says the RPD.

propositions.text: He left Rwanda in 2015, came to Canada, and claimed refugee protection weeks later.
propositions.quote: He left Rwanda on XXXX XXXX, 2015. He came to Canada and claimed refugee protection a few weeks later.

paragraphs.summary: He left Rwanda in 2015, came to Canada, and claimed refugee protection weeks later, says the RPD.

propositions.text: The RPD rejected the claim due to credibility issues from omissions, contradictions, inconsistencies, and implausibilities.
propositions.quote: On September 9, 2015, the RPD rejected his refugee protection claim, stating that [translation] "the claimant's credibility was the determinative issue" because of significant omissions, contradictions, inconsistencies and implausibilities.

propositions.text: RPD found it implausible that a government would offer training abroad to someone suspected of plotting against it.
propositions.quote: On this topic, the RPD found it implausible that a government which does not hesitate to eliminate its opponents would go as far as to offer training abroad to someone suspected of possessing information about a plot to overthrow the current regime;

propositions.text: RPD inferred negatively from omission of threat to life in initial BOC Form about 2015 attack.
propositions.quote: The RPD drew an inference from the omission in the initial BOC Form of a threat to his life by assailants during the alleged attack on XXXX XXXX, 2015;

propositions.text: RPD gave no probative value to medical report due to illegible signature, undated certificate, and reliance on claimant's words.
propositions.quote: The RPD granted no probative value to the medical report filed as Exhibit P-13 to corroborate the incident. The RPD noted that the physician's signature is illegible, the medical certificate is undated, and it does not mention the date on which the claimant was allegedly seen at the medical clinical. In short, it only reports the claimant's words;

propositions.text: Claimant failed to timely inform RPD that his wife fled to Kenya due to calls from local authority seeking him.
propositions.quote: The claimant failed to inform the RPD in a timely manner that his wife had left Rwanda to seek refuge in Kenya as she no longer felt comfortable because she was receiving calls from a local authority who was looking for the claimant;

propositions.text: RPD drew negative inference from omission of forced financial contributions to ruling party in BOC Form.
propositions.quote: The RPD drew a negative inference from the fact that the claimant omitted to include in his BOC Form that he had been forced to make financial contributions to the party in power for many years;

propositions.text: RPD found it implausible claimant left country easily while authorities allegedly sought to kill him.
propositions.quote: The RPD found it implausible that the claimant was able to leave his country without any difficulties while the authorities are allegedly looking for him and even want to kill him because he is suspected of having links to XXXX XXXX;

propositions.text: RPD found inconsistency that claimant's family remain in Rwanda without problems with regime.
propositions.quote: The RPD found it inconsistent that his parents, brothers and sisters are still in Rwanda and do not have any problems with the current regime;

propositions.text: RPD found risk to life inconsistent with claimant never hiding, moving, or changing phone number.
propositions.quote: The RPD found that the alleged risk to his life is inconsistent with the fact that the claimant never hid, moved or changed his telephone number;

propositions.text: RPD drew negative inference from claimant's 2012 stay in Kenya and return to Rwanda despite alleged torture in Rwanda.
propositions.quote: The RPD drew a negative inference from the fact that the claimant stayed in Kenya for three months in 2012 and returned to his country, while he alleged that he was tortured in a cell in Rwanda;

propositions.text: RPD believed claimant's ethnic origin is Banyamulenge but found it insufficient to conclude serious persecution risk.
propositions.quote: The RPD believed that his ethnic origin is Banyamulenge, but this element alone was not sufficient to conclude that he would face a serious possibility of persecution should he return to Rwanda.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD rejected the claim due to credibility issues, implausibilities, omissions, and inconsistencies, including doubts about training, medical report, family safety, and ethnic risk, says the RPD.

propositions.text: The appellant argues the RPD erred by not relying on evidence to contradict his testimony about his government position.
propositions.quote: With regard to his position in the Rwandan government, the appellant submits that the panel erred. According to him, RPD is not an organization that is [translation] "an expert on the Rwandan public service". The RPD [translation] "needed to rely on evidence indicating that the claimant's testimony did not correspond to the reality in Rwanda".

paragraphs.summary: The appellant argues the RPD erred by not relying on evidence to contradict his testimony about his government position.

propositions.text: The appellant argues the RPD's negative inference from omission of threats in BOC Form is exaggerated and illogical, as forgetting is human nature.
propositions.quote: Concerning the omission in the BOC Form that his assailants had threatened to kill him in the attack of XXXX XXXX, 2015, he argues that the conclusion is [translation] "clearly exaggerated and defies all logic". It is human nature to forget, and the fact that a person is educated and represented by counsel does not change the fact that the RPD made an error by drawing a negative inference regarding the omission in the initial BOC Form of the threats made by his assailants.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant argues the RPD's negative inference from omission of threats is exaggerated and illogical, as forgetting is human nature.

propositions.text: The appellant argues the RPD erred by dismissing the medical report due to illegible signature and undated certificate, which does not negate probative value.
propositions.quote: The appellant also submits that the RPD erred by not granting any probative value to the medical report. Counsel argues that the elements retained by the RPD, more specifically the fact that the physician's signature is illegible, [translation] "is the most far-fetched thing that the undersigned has read in quite a long time in an RPD determination. Frankly, this conclusion speaks for itself". Similarly, the fact that the physician reports the patient's statements about the circumstances in which he was injured, is [translation] "self-evident"; the physician was not there to be able to determine whether or not his patient was telling the truth.3 With regard to the fact that it was undated or that the date of the visit to the doctor was not indicated does not mean that the document has no probative value.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant argues the RPD erred by dismissing the medical report due to illegible signature and undated certificate, which does not negate probative value.

propositions.text: The appellant argues the RPD erred by drawing negative inferences from failure to discuss his wife and financial contributions to RPF in BOC Form.
propositions.quote: The panel also erred and its findings were unreasonable when it drew a negative inference from the fact that he failed to discuss his wife on his BOC Form. Moreover, he also did not indicate that he had contributed to the RPF (Rwandan Patriotic Front) when he worked for the XXXX XXXX XXXX4

paragraphs.summary: The appellant argues the RPD erred by drawing negative inferences from failure to discuss his wife and financial contributions to RPF in BOC Form.

propositions.text: The RAD must proceed de novo, assess evidence and draw conclusions without deference to the RPD, even on credibility findings.
propositions.quote: he submits that the RAD must proceed de novo, carry out its own assessment of the evidence and draw its own conclusions. It owes no deference to the RPD even when it is a matter of credibility findings.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant submits that the RAD must review the RPD decision de novo, independently assessing evidence and credibility without deference.

propositions.text: In Huruglica, the Federal Court of Appeal ruled that the RAD may use reasonableness standard for fact or mixed fact and law findings when credibility is not at issue.
propositions.quote: In Huruglica,5 the Federal Court of Appeal ruled on the issue of whether it was reasonable for the RAD, where credibility is not at issue, to examine findings of fact or of mixed fact and law using the standard of reasonableness.

paragraphs.summary: Huruglica ruled the RAD may apply reasonableness standard to fact or mixed fact and law findings when credibility is not at issue.

propositions.text: Justice Gauthier noted the RAD is a safety net to catch all RPD mistakes on law or facts.
propositions.quote: Justice Gauthier notes: [98] The RAD was essentially viewed as the safety net that would catch all mistakes made by the RPD, be it on the law or the facts.

paragraphs.summary: Justice Gauthier noted the RAD is intended as a safety net to catch all RPD errors on law or facts.

propositions.text: Sections 110 and 111 of IRPA require the RAD to intervene if the RPD decision is wrong in law, fact or mixed fact and law, applying a correctness standard.
propositions.quote: Paragraph 111(2)(a) does not distinguish between errors of law, fact or mixed fact and law. It simply requires that the decision of the RPD be "wrong in law, in fact or in mixed fact and law." ... This wording definitively points to the standard of correctness.

paragraphs.summary: The Court of Appeal states IRPA sections 110 and 111 require RAD to intervene if RPD decision is wrong in law, fact or mixed fact and law, using correctness standard.

propositions.text: The RAD's role is to intervene when the RPD is wrong in law, fact or mixed fact and law, applying correctness standard, but may confirm or substitute decision or refer back if needed.
propositions.quote: [78] ... [T]he role of the RAD is to intervene when the RPD is wrong in law, in fact or in fact and law. This translates into an application of the correctness standard of review. ... unless it is satisfied that it cannot do either without hearing the evidence presented to the RPD: paragraph 111(2)(b) of the IRPA.

paragraphs.summary: The Court of Appeal says RAD must intervene if RPD is wrong, applying correctness standard, but may confirm, substitute or refer back if evidence hearing needed.

propositions.text: Justice Gauthier stated RAD reviews RPD findings of fact or mixed fact and law without credibility issues using correctness standard, conducting own analysis and providing final determination.
propositions.quote: [103] ... [W]ith respect to findings of fact (and mixed fact and law) such as the one involved here, which raised no issue of credibility of oral evidence, the RAD is to review RPD decisions applying the correctness standard. ... It is only when the RAD is of the opinion that it cannot provide such a final determination without hearing the oral evidence presented to the RPD that the matter can be referred back to the RPD for redetermination.

paragraphs.summary: Justice Gauthier stated RAD reviews RPD fact or mixed fact and law findings without credibility issues using correctness standard and own analysis, referring back only if oral evidence needed.

propositions.text: I will independently assess the evidence and determine if the RPD decision is correct, intervening if errors of fact, law or mixed fact and law exist.
propositions.quote: I will conduct an independent assessment of the evidence in order to formulate my own opinion on this refugee protection claim and to determine whether the decision is correct. If an error of fact, of law or of mixed law and fact was made, I will intervene using one of the remedies set out in sections 110 and 111 of the IRPA.

paragraphs.summary: I will independently assess the evidence and decide if the RPD decision is correct, intervening if errors exist.

propositions.text: The RPD found the claimant was not credible or trustworthy on central claim elements.
propositions.quote: The RPD was of the opinion that the claimant did not establish that he is a credible and trustworthy witness with respect to the central elements in his claim.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found the claimant not credible or trustworthy on central claim elements.

propositions.text: The Federal Court of Appeal in Huruglica acknowledged the RPD may have advantage over RAD in fact findings requiring oral evidence weight assessment; RAD must decide if it can decide or must refer back.
propositions.quote: In Huruglica,6 the Federal Court of Appeal acknowledges that there may be cases where the RPD enjoys an advantage over the RAD in making findings of fact or mixed fact and law, because they require assessment of the weight to be given to the oral evidence it hears. ... the RAD must determine whether, in light of the evidence, it can make a final decision or must send the matter to the RPD.

paragraphs.summary: Huruglica acknowledged RPD may have advantage in fact findings involving oral evidence weight; RAD must decide if it can decide or refer back.

propositions.text: The claimant's negative credibility finding is based on several elements; even if one is wrong, the decision is appropriate.
propositions.quote: The claimant's negative credibility finding is based on several elements. Even if I am of the opinion that one of them may be wrong, I find that the decision rendered is the appropriate one in the circumstances.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant's negative credibility finding rests on several elements; even if one is wrong, the decision is appropriate.

propositions.text: The RPD found the claimant's allegations contradicted his long career and found it implausible he would be sent to Kenya for training given his opposition to the regime and torture history.
propositions.quote: The RPD is of the opinion that the claimant's allegations "clearly contradicted the claimant's remarkable and long career of many years" ... It is implausible and not credible ... he would be sent to Kenya for training.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found the claimant's allegations contradicted his career and found it implausible he would be sent to Kenya for training given his opposition and torture history.

propositions.text: The RPD erred by concluding without evidence that the claimant's testimony did not correspond to reality; unusual situations are possible.
propositions.quote: The appellant argued that the RPD erred by reaching this conclusion and that it "needed evidence on which it could rely indicating that the claimant's testimony did not correspond to the reality in Rwanda. ... there are many cases of persons who have opinions contrary to those of their supervisors holding a position in a given institution".

paragraphs.summary: The appellant argues the RPD erred by concluding without evidence that his testimony was not real; unusual situations can occur.

propositions.text: I agree with the RPD that the claimant's situation is implausible given Rwanda's political context and severe punishment of dissent.
propositions.quote: With all due respect for the submissions, I share the opinion of the RPD. ... the RPD was correct in this case. ... the assessment of credibility should take into account the social and political context in Rwanda ... where any dissent is severely punished.

paragraphs.summary: I agree with the RPD that the claimant's situation is implausible given Rwanda's political context and severe dissent punishment.

propositions.text: The Federal Court of Appeal in Aguebor held that a panel need not accept uncontradicted testimony and may rely on reason, common sense and rationality.
propositions.quote: As stated by the Federal Court of Appeal in Aguebor,10 ... The panel is not under any obligation to accept testimony simply because it was not contradicted. It can base its decision on reason, common sense and rationality.

paragraphs.summary: Aguebor held panels need not accept uncontradicted testimony and may rely on reason, common sense and rationality.

propositions.text: The alleged situation is implausible and not credible when considered as a whole and in context.
propositions.quote: In this case, the alleged situation considered as a whole and in its context is implausible and even not credible.

paragraphs.summary: The alleged situation is implausible and not credible when considered as a whole and in context.

propositions.text: The appellant was held and tortured in 2010 to supply information about an alleged plot to overthrow the government.
propositions.quote: The appellant submitted that he had been held in a cell and tortured in 2010 so that he would supply information about an alleged plot planned by XXXX XXXX to overthrow the government.

propositions.text: It would be illogical for the regime to offer training abroad to someone suspected of ties to opposition and torture.
propositions.quote: it would be illogical for the XXXX in place that suspects the claimant of having ties with the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, to offer him training abroad, allowing him to advance his career.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant says he was tortured in 2010 over a plot; I find it illogical the regime would offer training abroad to a suspected opposition link.

propositions.text: The appellant's return to Rwanda after training in Kenya contradicts his claim that his life was at risk there.
propositions.quote: In the same vein, the appellant's return to Rwanda after three months of training in Kenya contradicts the credibility of his allegations that his life was at risk in Rwanda.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant's return to Rwanda after Kenya training contradicts his claim his life was at risk there.

propositions.text: The appellant testified he tried to leave Rwanda but could not get a scholarship to study in Holland; documents confirm admission to a school in 2010.
propositions.quote: When questioned about it, the appellant testified at the hearing that he tried to leave the country, but he was unable to obtain a scholarship allowing him to study in Holland. The documents in the RPD file confirm that the appellant was admitted to the XXXX School of XXXX in XXXX 2010.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant testified he tried to leave Rwanda but failed to get a Holland scholarship; documents confirm his 2010 school admission.

propositions.text: The appellant claims he was tortured in 2010 for imputed political opinion and fears returning for the same reason.
propositions.quote: The appellant claims that he was tortured in XXXX 2010 by reason of imputed political opinion, the same reason he fears returning to Rwanda today.

propositions.text: The appellant has not established subjective fear of persecution for political opinion under section 96 IRPA, a fatal flaw warranting dismissal.
propositions.quote: Based on various decisions of the Federal Court, I would add that under section 96 of the IRPA, the appellant has not established his subjective fear of persecution by reason of "real or perceived political opinion." ... The lack of evidence going to the subjective element of the claim is a fatal flaw which in and of itself warrants dismissal of the claim.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant claims torture and fear for political opinion, but has not established subjective fear, a fatal flaw warranting dismissal.

propositions.text: The appellant's return to Rwanda and explanations undermine his credibility and detention claim; the RPD was correct to dismiss his claim.
propositions.quote: It is also my opinion because of this return to Rwanda, his allegations that his life is at risk under section 97 of the IRPA for the alleged reasons are not credible. It also casts serious doubt on his detention in XXXX 2010. ... the RPD was correct to dismiss his explanations ...

paragraphs.summary: The appellant's return to Rwanda and explanations undermine his credibility and detention claim; the RPD was correct to dismiss his claim.

propositions.text: The RPD identified omissions on the BOC Form about threats to life, wife's safety concerns, and forced contributions to RPF.
propositions.quote: The RPD identified several omissions on the BOC Form. Specifically, it noted that the claimant failed to indicate that his life was threatened in the attack on XXXX XXXX XXXX 2015, that his wife left Rwanda because she did not feel safe, and that he was forced to make contributions to the RPF (the party in power).

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found omissions on the BOC Form about threats to life, wife's safety, and forced contributions to RPF.

propositions.text: The determinative omissions were threats to life and wife's departure due to safety concerns from local authority inquiries.
propositions.quote: In my opinion, the determinative omissions were the threats to his life and the fact that his spouse left Rwanda as she did not feel safe because a local authority was asking about her husband.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the key omissions were threats to life and wife's unsafe departure due to local authority inquiries.

propositions.text: The RPD drew a negative inference from omission of death threats in initial BOC Form despite their addition in amended form.
propositions.quote: Considering the significance of this fact, the RPD draws a negative inference, even though the appellant added it to his amended BOC Form.

propositions.text: The appellant alleged he received death threats during the 2015 attack, which were not initially mentioned.
propositions.quote: The appellant alleged that he received death threats when he was allegedly attacked in XXXX 2015. These death threats were not mentioned in the initial BOC Form.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant alleges death threats in 2015 attack; the RPD draws negative inference from their omission in initial BOC Form.

propositions.text: The appellant argues omission of exact words at attack was an oversight, not intent to lie, and exaggeration by RPD.
propositions.quote: The appellant submits [translation] "the implication that he intended to lie to the panel because of the fact that he did not include the words said to him at the time of the attack on XXXX XXXX, 2015, is clearly exaggerated and defies all logic." Apparently, it was an oversight on his part.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant argues omission of exact words at attack was oversight, not intent to lie, and RPD's implication is exaggerated.

propositions.text: The RPD may consider omissions in BOC Form and draw negative credibility inferences from important facts added only by amendment.
propositions.quote: It is well established that the panel is entitled to consider the contents of the Personal Information Form (PIF) before and after it has been amended, and the panel may also draw negative conclusions about the claimant's credibility when matters considered important are included in the PIF by amendment at the hearing.

propositions.text: Omitting death threats in initial BOC Form justified RPD's negative inference; death threats are significant facts.
propositions.quote: In my opinion, death threats are not insignificant. The RPD was justified in drawing a negative inference from this omission on the initial BOC Form.

propositions.text: Omitting assailants' words is less serious than omitting death threats.
propositions.quote: In my opinion, the fact that he did not indicate in his BOC Form the words of his alleged assailants is one thing, but completely omitting that he was threatened with death is another.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds RPD justified in negative inference from omission of death threats, a significant fact, in initial BOC Form.

propositions.text: The RPD drew a negative inference from omission that appellant's wife left Rwanda due to safety concerns.
propositions.quote: The RPD also drew a negative inference from the fact that the appellant did not mention in the BOC Form or the amended BOC Form that his wife had left the country as she no longer felt safe because of him.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD drew negative inference from omission that appellant's wife left Rwanda for safety reasons.

propositions.text: The appellant did not mention in BOC Form that local authority asked his wife about him, despite testifying to it at hearing.
propositions.quote: The claimant did not mention this fact in his BOC Form, which he amended twice.

propositions.text: At hearing, appellant testified local authority asked his wife about him.
propositions.quote: At the hearing, the appellant testified that the XXXX XXXX XXXX had asked his wife about him.

propositions.text: The RPD may consider omissions from amended BOC Form in assessing credibility.
propositions.quote: The RPD may consider the omission of this element from the amended BOC Form.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant testified local authority asked his wife about him; RPD may consider omission of this fact from amended BOC Form.

propositions.text: The court disagrees with RPD that medical certificate lacks probative value due to illegible signature and no date.
propositions.quote: I do not share the RPD's opinion when it determines that the document has no probative value because the physician's signature is illegible and it is undated, among other things.

propositions.text: The RPD should have questioned claimant about circumstances and reasons for medical certificate.
propositions.quote: In my opinion, the RPD should have questioned the claimant to find out in which circumstances and for what reasons the certificate was issued.

propositions.text: The medical certificate alone is insufficient to prove attack reasons or CID officers' involvement.
propositions.quote: Having said that, I am of the opinion that this certificate alone is insufficient to establish that the claimant was attacked for the alleged reasons or that CID officers were at the origin of the attack.

paragraphs.summary: The court disagrees with RPD's dismissal of medical certificate but finds it alone insufficient to prove attack reasons or CID involvement.

propositions.text: The RPD drew negative inference from claimant living at same address despite alleged authorities' search since 2010.
propositions.quote: The RPD drew a negative inference from the fact that the claimant continued to live at the same address until he left the country in 2015, when he alleged that the authorities had been looking for him since XXXX 2010.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD drew negative inference from claimant living at same address despite alleged authorities' search since 2010.

propositions.text: IRB may consider claimant's conduct facing risk; serious fear would prompt moving or job change at first opportunity.
propositions.quote: In Ramirez,19 Justice Shore states that the IRB may take into account a claimant's conduct in the face of alleged risk. If he seriously feared persecution or his life was at risk, he would have moved or changed jobs at the first opportunity.

paragraphs.summary: Justice Shore in Ramirez states IRB may consider claimant's conduct; serious fear would cause moving or job change promptly.

propositions.text: Claimant's CV and Form IMM-5669 conflict on employment dates and job titles, undermining credibility of job change claim.
propositions.quote: Even though the claimant indicated that he changed jobs in XXXX 2014 to get away from his problems, a review of his curriculum vitae compared with the information on Form IMM-5669 shows that he worked for the XXXX XXXX Company from XXXX 2013 until he left the country in XXXX 2015, whereas the information in his curriculum vitae indicates that he had worked as a "XXXX XXXX in XXXX XXXX XXXX." since XXXX 2012 and, at the time of preparing his curriculum vitae , which seemed to be in XXXX 2015, and he was still working there.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds claimant's CV and form conflict on employment, undermining his job change claim.

propositions.text: Documentary evidence on Banyamulenge treatment insufficient to show claimant faces serious persecution risk; family has no particular problems.
propositions.quote: In this context, given the profile of a refugee protection claimant, it is my opinion that the documentary evidence regarding the treatment of the Banyamulenge is insufficient to find that the claimant runs serious risk of persecution in the event of his return to Rwanda; his testimony established that his family does not have any particular problems as a result of this fact.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds evidence insufficient to show claimant faces serious persecution risk; family has no particular problems.

propositions.text: Claimant has not established serious possibility of persecution or likely risk to life on return on balance of evidence.
propositions.quote: I consider these elements sufficient to find that the refugee protection claimant has not established the alleged facts on the balance of the evidence and, therefore, has not established neither a serious possibility of persecution nor that it is likely that his life would be at risk should he return.

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes claimant has not established serious persecution possibility or life risk on return.

propositions.text: The court confirms RPD's decision that claimant is neither Convention refugee nor person in need of protection under IRPA sections 96 and 97.
propositions.quote: I confirm the RPD's determination that XXXX XXXX XXXX is neither a "Convention refugee" under section 96 of the IRPA nor a "person in need of protection" under section 97 of the IRPA.

paragraphs.summary: The court confirms RPD's decision claimant is neither Convention refugee nor person in need of protection under IRPA.

propositions.text: The appeal is dismissed.
propositions.quote: The appeal is dismissed.

paragraphs.summary: The court dismisses the appeal.
